tools.blocked_reason:
DUPLICATED BY AN ALWAYS-ON CONSUMER-LOCAL TOOL THAT RETURNS THE SAME 12 ROWS. Not a selection failure and not a model failure - measured, the model gave the user a complete and correct answer using the tool the platform puts in front of it.

Asked 'What workflows are available to me?', the model called workflow_list on 5 of 5 runs and never registry_list_workflows. The gate's own DATA bars pass on that evidence, including 'answer is true' - because the answer WAS true.

THE TWO TOOLS ARE THE SAME CAPABILITY, checked rather than assumed:
  registry_list_workflows (federated, Tier R) - 'List the curated multi-step workflows visible to the signed-in user (System defaults + their own). Returns each workflow's slug + title + description.'
  workflow_list (CONSUMER-LOCAL, WS-2b, dispatched inside stream_service) - 'enumerate the curated workflows visible this turn (slug/title/description)'.
Called directly over MCP, registry_list_workflows returns count=12 with slugs [autonomous-drafting, build-a-book, canon-check, chapter-compose, draw-a-map, entity-triage, glossary-bootstrap, kg-build, lore-so-far, populate-from-notes, translation-pass, vision-to-book]. workflow_list returned count=12 in every run. Same shape, same size, same data.

🔴 THE TURN-SCOPED WORDING LOOKED LIKE A DEFECT AND IS NOT. 'visible THIS TURN' against 'visible to the signed-in user' is exactly the shape of an incomplete answer to a broader question, so it was worth checking whether the user was shown fewer workflows than they own. They were not: both denominators are 12 today. Recorded because the NEXT reader will have the same suspicion, and because the two could diverge the moment a turn-scoped curation actually narrows.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE TOOL. registry_list_workflows is unreachable on the chat surface by construction: its consumer-local twin is in the ALWAYS-ON CORE, so it is advertised on every pass of every turn, while the federated tool has to win a hot-seed slot. A user's words cannot separate them - they answer the same question. It declares no superseded_by, which is the inverse of DQ-T2's complaint (55 legacy tools that declare deprecation and name no successor): here is a tool that is superseded in practice and says nothing.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE OWNER, not a decision: either mark it superseded_by workflow_list so discovery stops offering both, or give workflow_list a narrower name and description so the two denominators are distinguishable from the surface. Leaving it as-is means one of the two is dead weight on every catalogue sweep this loop runs.

SHIP cases stay unexercised through the measured path; it has never been called there.

Measured against the deployed matcher for 'What workflows are available to me?': R1 forces EXACTLY ONE tool, registry_list_workflows. Its twin workflow_list is NOT IN THE FEDERATED CATALOGUE at all — it is a consumer-local meta tool (_CONSUMER_LOCAL_META_TOOLS), with its def in workflow_runner.WORKFLOW_LIST_TOOL and dispatch inside stream_service.

🔴 So it is NOT 'in the ALWAYS-ON CORE': ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES, read from the running service, is exactly (tool_list, tool_load, confirm_action, web_search). The conclusion was right and the mechanism was not, which matters because nothing about ALWAYS_ON_CORE_NAMES would change this.

The general property is that answerability ranks over the FEDERATED catalogue, so a consumer-local tool that duplicates a federated one is invisible to it and wins unconditionally. Recorded as D-ANSWERABILITY-IS-BLIND-TO-CONSUMER-LOCAL-TOOLS.

tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED on D-LIVE-INVENTORY-ANSWERED-FROM-THE-REGISTRY, which is NOT fixed and would have passed this gate silently. Surfaced 5/5, called 1/5 — up from 0/5 after the description now states that this tool's LIVE inventory differs from settings_list_models' REGISTERED set, so the declaration moved the behaviour. It did not move it far enough.

On the ONE run that called it, the model chained settings_list_providers -> settings_provider_inventory and described the result truthfully as 'currently registered'. On the OTHER FOUR it called settings_list_models alone and told the author 'here is the breakdown of what your providers currently offer' — registry rows presented as live inventory, the exact false statement this tool is blocked for.

🔴 THE GATE WOULD HAVE PASSED IT. LIVE requires called >= 1 and it was called once; answer_expect was NULL so the 'DATA answer is true' bar never ran; and the falsifier covers a store change and unconfigured providers, not this. A declared expectation is added here that discriminates perfectly on the measured runs, so the next run cannot pass while the author is still being misled 4 times in 5.

CONTROL: the model must find map_id itself (world_map_list) — a turn that never lists is a DISCOVERY failure, not a failure of this tool.
